content: {"id": "054cff8a-798d-4807-bcab-5d23a713393a", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "For an AWS Config resource type that changes many times per day, which recording mode is usually cheaper - continuous or daily - and why? No account access required.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "c3185cbc-11fd-4b50-adde-8b7da14ec412", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "For a resource type that changes many times per day, **daily recording is almost always cheaper** — and often by a wide margin.

Here's why:

- **Continuous recording** bills a configuration item (CI) every time the resource's configuration changes. If a resource type churns many times per day (e.g., ECS task state, frequently-updated security groups, autoscaling group membership), you're paying for every single one of those changes as a separate billable CI.
- **Daily recording** collapses all of that churn into a **single configuration item per resource per day**, regardless of how many times it actually changed. You get one snapshot capturing the latest state, once every 24 hours.

So the cost driver is change frequency: continuous mode's cost scales with the *number of changes*, while daily mode's cost is flat — one CI per resource per day no matter how noisy it is. For a high-churn resource type, continuous can generate 10s–100s of billable CIs a day per resource, while daily generates exactly 1. That's the classic "high-churn driver" pattern config-cost reviews look for.

The trade-off is fidelity: with daily recording you lose the intermediate change history within that 24-hour window — you only get end-of-day state, not every transition. So it's cheaper but coarser. If you need to catch transient or intra-day configuration changes for compliance/audit reasons, continuous is still necessary despite the cost; otherwise daily is the more economical choice for chatty resource types.

If you want, I can run a cost-optimization pass against your actual Config setup to see which of your resource types are high-churn and would benefit from switching to daily recording.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
